original_query: SELECT MGR, SUM(SUM_SAL) FROM (SELECT MGR, SUM(SAL) AS SUM_SAL FROM EMP GROUP BY MGR, DEPTNO HAVING DEPTNO = 100) AS t2 GROUP BY MGR
rewritten_query:
SELECT MGR, SUM(SAL)
FROM EMP
WHERE DEPTNO = 100
GROUP BY MGR

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Move the HAVING DEPTNO = 100 filter into a WHERE clause so rows are filtered before grouping, reducing the number of rows entering the aggregate.
Remove the derived table t2. Since DEPTNO is fixed at 100, the inner GROUP BY (MGR, DEPTNO) yields one row per MGR, making the outer SUM aggregation redundant; collapse into a single GROUP BY MGR.

Given EMP has ~45M rows, consider a covering index on (DEPTNO, MGR) INCLUDE (SAL) if DEPTNO = 100 is selective, enabling an index-only scan and pre-sorted grouping. Avoid unnecessary CTEs for this simple query.
